recentItems.title: Russia parliamentary elections: 10 parties compete amid war in Ukraine
recentItems.description:
Russia heads to parliamentary elections as political competition remains tightly controlled. With major parties backing the Kremlin’s policies and the war in Ukraine, the vote is expected to largely preserve the current political balance.

Al Jazeera’s Dmitry Medvedenk Oreports.

recentItems.title: China domestic crude: Conflicts in middle east pushed prices record high
recentItems.description:
Global oil price increases are driving up fuel prices in China amid disruptions to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. Despite higher prices, China faces no immediate oil shortage, thanks to its large reserves and diversified import sources.

Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu has reports.

recentItems.title: Occupied west bank violence: Israeli army "helping settlers displace Palestinians"
recentItems.description:

Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh reports.

recentItems.title: Political killings spark fear in South Africa ahead of local elections
recentItems.description:
A rise in political killings in South Africa is raising fears that November’s local elections could be among the most violent yet.
One study shows at least 26 people were killed in suspected political attacks in the first seven months of the year.
Some officials believe the violence is being used to reduce competition for sought after councillor positions.

Al Jazeera’s Haru Mutasa reports from Eshowe in KwaZulu-Natal, one of the most affected provinces.

recentItems.title: US Veteran told he is ‘embarrassing’ uniform over Israeli bonds stance
recentItems.description:
A veteran was told he is ‘embarrassing’ his uniform for protesting Palm Beach County’s $1B investment in Israel bonds. The exchange took place during a heated council meeting as residents voiced outrage over the record investment.
